instrument_fault_found_by_the_specialist.judge_action: Fixed, because the judge owns instruments. The assertion now checks the RULE the test exists to guard rather than a copied number: no coin may pick the blank (r 47), the blank must be seen and REJECTED where it is a candidate, and all coins must agree on one radius since EDGE is one shared value. It now passes and prints "(blank offered and rejected)" on exactly the penny and the nickel — the two coins v1 got wrong. An assertion about a constant should name the constant or check the property, never copy the value.

instrument_faults_reported_and_NOT_fixed: textMarks() collapses a whole flat legend to a single 0.62*size glyph box centred on the <text> anchor, so MONTICELLO, the dime's E PLURIBUS UNUM and now the cent's two lines each contribute one ~3.4-unit box rather than their true 16-56 unit extent. D8 is therefore blind to a flat legend's horizontal reach. Pre-existing; it does not bite here (the cent's true ink corner is r 33.3 against 44.07) but it would on a wide flat legend near the rim.

nickel-rev-2.png has a mathematically FLAT field: every 5x5 patch on the disc interior returns MAD 0.000, so any threshold derived as k*sigma is 0 and the whole window becomes ink. The specialist floored sigma at 1.0 grey and prints a warning when the floor binds. Worth knowing for any future tone or edge instrument pointed at that reference.

The specialist's own response test showed the cent legend's CAP TOP is rock stable (19.400 across k=4,5,6 and half sampling step) while its FOOT is not (24.500 -> 23.650 -> 23.600), because the relief drop shadow sits below the letters. It took the baseline from the median of clean per-glyph runs and said which edge is soft. That is the standard.

kind: RETRACTION-BESIDE — the judge's own candidate fix for D13 FAILED its test
retracts: the entry appended earlier today under "judge finding — the tone acquisition landed, and D13 has a candidate fix", which proposed field level = the MODE of the interior histogram and reported it as "the better estimator" that "removes the per-design literals".
status: NOT ADOPTED. The proposal is wrong and v1 stands unchanged.
what_went_wrong: The premise — "the field is the largest single-tone region on any struck coin" — is true of a COIN and false of the LOCUS this metric uses. Inside r < 40 at the icon tier the DEVICE covers most of the interior, so the mode is the device. Measured on our own renders at 26px, the fraction of interior pixels within two grey levels of p90 (i.e. plausibly field): penny obverse 0.13, dime obverse 0.17, nickel obverse 0.23, quarter reverse 0.26, quarter obverse 0.27, penny reverse 0.37 — against nickel reverse 0.52 and dime reverse 0.41, the only two faces where the mode really is the field. SIX OF EIGHT FACES WOULD HAVE DIVIDED BY THE DEVICE.
the_symptom_that_exposed_it: v2 swings delta mean/field positive on almost every face (+0.17 to +0.41) and FAILS MORE faces than v1. A normaliser change of 7% on the reference side cannot move a ratio that far; the movement was on OUR side, because our mode is the bust tone and our p90 is the field.
why_the_earlier_validation_missed_it: It tested the mode only against REVERSE references — dime-rev-2, dime-rev-unc2005, dime-rev-proofbright, nickel-rev-2 — which are exactly the cases where the field does dominate. A validation set containing only the cases where a rule holds is not a validation, and I built one and then quoted its agreement as evidence.
what_survives: The DIAGNOSIS of v1 is untouched and still measured: on three of four reverse references the p90 is a specular highlight on the device, the reference's own bare field is classified as ink, and delta is biased by the photograph's lighting. Both normalisers are wrong, for opposite reasons, and NEITHER is a field level. D13 therefore remains ESCALATED, and the numbers in every scorecard remain v1's.
the_consequence_that_is_new: A sound normaliser needs a locus where field actually dominates — an annulus clear of the device and clear of the legend band — and where that annulus lies is a fact about each design, which is a SEGMENTATION. D2 is BLOCKED on exactly that. This is now demonstrated rather than suspected: D13 and D2 are blocked on one missing capability, and buying it once buys both.
instrument: coloringbook/judge/_jd13v2.mjs — kept, as the evidence for this finding rather than as a fix. It prints both normalisers side by side and its header records the failure.

kind: RETRACTION-BESIDE — v1.57.0 moved D10 on every obverse and the judge did not measure it

measured.instrument: _jp10tier.mjs, obverse, 42->44 boundary, absolute d(ink) beside the ratio per Appendix R2
measured.method: the same instrument run against the v1.56.0 art via its own ART env override, so the only variable is the drawing

the_honest_shape_of_it: It is NOT "v1.57.0 broke D10". Across the four coins it went two ways: the cent 5.44 -> 24.64 and the quarter 6.36 -> 12.43 got much worse, while the nickel 24.21 -> 9.12 and the dime 5.56 -> 4.26 got better. Which way a coin moved depends on how close its icon-tier ink already was to its mid-tier ink, which is a property of that coin's bust. ALL FOUR STILL FAIL the 4x gate, before and after. What is squarely mine is that a change I made moved a gated dimension on all eight faces in both directions and I published a round entry naming the dimensions I had checked without noticing D10 was absent from it.
how_it_was_caught: Not by me. The round-5 specialist was told to re-derive the brief's figures before acting, found D10-obverse at 24.64x against a published 5.44x, and attributed it to the field change. I then measured all four coins against the v1.56.0 art to establish the blast radius.
consequences: D10 is now part of the standing must-not-regress set in _rescore.mjs, where D8/D9/D11 already were. A dimension that is not in the re-derivation set is a dimension nobody is watching.

The candidate repair is to reconsider EDGE.field.icon = 42.5, since the step IS the discontinuity. That is a shared constant touching all four coins, so it cannot go in a parallel round (COIN-JUDGE 5 as amended today) and is queued as a serialised judge round.

Appendix R2 is vindicated twice over: the absolute numerator moved every time, so none of this is a denominator artefact, and reporting the numerator beside the ratio is what makes the two-directional result legible at all.

kind: judge finding — D10's RATIO depends on an undeclared sweep locus, and two live instruments disagree
measured: On the nickel obverse, same tree, same drawing: _jp10tier.mjs reports 9.12x and _jn8tier.mjs reports 4.93x. The NUMERATOR is identical in both (d(ink) 0.0854) and so is d(mean) (0.0242). The whole difference is the denominator — the within-tier p90 — because the two instruments sweep different size ranges (n=85 samples vs n=45).
why_it_matters: Section 6.1: a gate needs a LOCUS, not just a threshold, and the locus is frozen with the target rather than chosen at measuring time. D10's threshold (4x) is declared; its sweep is not, and the ratio moves 1.85x depending on which instrument runs. Every D10 verdict on every coin inherits that.
a_comparison_the_judge_got_wrong: My blast-radius table quoted the nickel as 24.21x -> 9.12x. The 24.21 came from _jn8tier (round 0) and the 9.12 from _jp10tier — two instruments. Like for like through _jn8tier it is 24.21 -> 4.93; like for like through _jp10tier it is 24.21 -> 9.12, the two agreeing at v1.56.0 and diverging since. The direction of the finding stands; the precise figure was a mixed comparison.
also: A second validity limit: _jn8tier's field level is a 90th percentile, and at icon fill 0.859 it recovers FIVE different field levels instead of one, because the device covers too much of the sampling disc for p90 to be bare field. Its own bug-report line catches it; the limit is undocumented. This is the same failure class as D13's normaliser.
queued: Declare one D10 sweep locus and re-score every coin against it, with retractions beside the published figures. Serialised judge round.

kind: ESCALATION — D7's metric returns 90 degrees for a perfectly smooth curve
finding: _jqgeom.turns() measures the angle between CHORDS joining consecutive on-curve knots. That is a property of how far apart the knots are, not of whether the curve kinks.
judge_verification: Re-derived independently, not taken on report. A G1-continuous join of two half-circles, sampled as knots, returns a worst CHORD turn of 90.0 degrees; sampled coarsely at 5 knots the same smooth curve returns 116.6. The tangent estimator returns 0.0 on the same path.
why_it_survived: quarter-gates.md's stated response test is "a synthetic path with a known 90-degree corner reports 90 +- 1". BOTH estimators pass that test, so it cannot distinguish them. A response test that every candidate passes is not a discriminator — Appendix P/Q's lesson, in a new place.
what_it_invalidates: Every D7 verdict on every coin, across four rounds. Specifically it includes the DIME'S D7 PASS accepted in v1.61.0, which turned a FAIL into a PASS by declaring a 111-degree chord knot an authored corner.
what_survives_and_why: The per-knot DECLARATIONS remain defensible as RELATIVE statements, because each compared our chord turn against the TARGET MASK'S chord turn at the same place with a known-straight control — like against like, same estimator both sides. The dime's reads our 110.97 against the mask's 99-122 with a straight-cut control at 6.4-37.9, and that comparison still says the die cuts a corner there. What does NOT survive is the ABSOLUTE gate: "0 knots turning more than 75 degrees" is not a statement about curvature.
status: D7 is ESCALATED on all four coins, alongside D13 (normaliser measures the photograph's lighting) and D2 (thresholded masks record lighting as shape). Section 8: the honest verdict is ESCALATE, never a relaxed gate.

kind: SERIALISED JUDGE ROUND — D7 re-stated on tangent discontinuity, with a retraction
the_fault_restated: _jqgeom.turns() measures the angle between CHORDS joining consecutive on-curve knots — a property of knot SPACING, not of whether the curve kinks. Verified twice independently: a G1-continuous join of two half-circles returns a worst chord turn of 90.0 degrees (116.6 sampled coarsely) where the tangent measure returns 0.0.
why_it_survived_four_rounds: The gate's stated response test is "a synthetic path with a known 90 degree corner reports 90 +- 1". BOTH estimators pass it, so it could never discriminate. The new instrument's test set adds the case that does: a G1-smooth join with the knots far apart, where the sound measure reads 0.0 and the unsound one reads 90.0.
new_instrument: coloringbook/judge/_jd7tan.mjs — parses the control points off the emitted `d` strings (which flattenPath discards), computes the tangent discontinuity at every join INCLUDING THE CLOSURE KNOT that turns() never evaluates, and prints the chord number beside it on every row so nothing is silently replaced. Response tests: known 90-degree tangent kink -> 90.0; G1-smooth join -> 0.0 tangent / 90.0 chord; straight run -> 0.0 / 0.0. Arcs are COUNTED and reported rather than scored as zero.

re_derived_both_measures.note: worst angle and count over 75 degrees, at size 380, over EVERY path the face emits

THE_FINDING_IS_NOT_WHAT_I_EXPECTED: The two measures disagree IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, so neither is a refinement of the other. The note's obverse is the cleanest demonstration of the fault — chord 71.0 against tangent 1.2, i.e. a face the old metric put just under its gate is in truth almost perfectly smooth. But the dime reverse goes the other way: 81 knots over 75 by chord and 123 by tangent. A chord can HIDE a real kink as well as invent one, wherever the control legs are short relative to the chord. Every published D7 verdict therefore needs re-deriving on the sound measure; it is not enough to assume the old numbers were pessimistic.
RETRACTS: Every published D7 figure on every coin and side, across four rounds — including the dime obverse PASS accepted in v1.61.0, which turned a FAIL into a PASS by declaring a 111-degree CHORD knot an authored corner.
what_survives: The per-knot DECLARATIONS remain defensible as relative statements, because each compared our chord turn against the TARGET MASK'S chord turn at the same place with a known-straight control — like against like, same estimator on both sides. The dime's reads our 110.97 against the mask's 99-122 with a straight-cut control at 6.4-37.9, and that still says the die cuts a corner there. What does not survive is the ABSOLUTE gate: "0 knots turning more than 75 degrees" was never a statement about curvature.
WHAT_IS_STILL_OWED_AND_WHY_THIS_IS_NOT_A: The sweep above scores EVERY path a face emits, while P2 restricts D7 to paths produced by FITTING a contour — an authored polygon declares its corners and those knots are exempt. So these numbers are a superset and are NOT directly comparable to the published per-coin figures, which were fitted-contour only. Completing the re-score needs the fitted/authored partition applied per coin, which each scorecard names individually. Stating that limit rather than presenting the sweep as a finished verdict.

kind: SERIALISED JUDGE ROUND — D7 re-scored on FITTED CONTOURS ONLY, completing the escalation
what_was_owed: The first re-derivation scored every path a face emits, while Appendix P2 restricts D7 to paths produced by FITTING a contour. This finishes it: HEAD, HAIR and BEARD are the constants _pybuild.mjs fits from the frozen masks, identified by matching their geometry against the emitted `d` rather than by any name in the SVG.
WHAT_IT_MEANS: THE CENT'S HAIR IS SMOOTH. HAIR.Lincoln reads chord 144.5 with 2 knots over 75, and tangent 1.0 with NONE. Round 5 spent an entire round establishing those two knots as authored corners — mask readings, a chord estimator with synthetic 90/0 controls, ray fans on the photograph, a declaration written into coins.js. That work was careful and it was unnecessary: the knots never kinked. They were an artefact of measuring a curve by the polygon through its knots.
THE NICKEL'S HAIR IS SMOOTH TOO: chord 173.0 (1 over) against tangent 14.0 (none).

THE QUARTER'S HAIR IS SMOOTH: chord 102.0 (1 over) against tangent 1.2. That is the knot round 8 was told, on my authority, had been "confirmed by eye as a visible kink". It has a tangent discontinuity of 1.2 degrees. Round 8 measured it at 0.4 and called the claim contradicted; this confirms it independently.

THE DIME'S IS REAL. HEAD.Roosevelt reads 111.0 by chord and 111.2 by tangent — the two agree, so knot 23 is a genuine 111-degree tangent discontinuity. Round 4's declaration therefore STANDS on its own evidence (the frozen mask turns 99-122 degrees there against a straight-cut control at 6.4-37.9): it is a corner the die cuts, and it is exempt because it is declared, not because the metric was wrong.
A_FAILURE_NOBODY_HAD_SEEN: HAIR.Roosevelt carries THREE genuine tangent kinks — 156.3 at the closure knot, 114.9 at knot 16, 84.8 at knot 30 — and it has never been scored. The dime's published D7 locus is "FITTED HEAD" only; its hair was never in the subject set. So the dime obverse has a real, undeclared D7 failure that four rounds of scoring could not have found, because the locus omitted the path.
the_net_effect_on_verdicts: Three of the four coins PASS D7 on fitted contours under the sound measure with no declarations needed at all. The dime fails, once by a declared and defensible corner and once by three undeclared kinks on a path nobody was scoring. The published figures were not uniformly pessimistic — they were unrelated to curvature, and happened to be conservative on three coins and blind on the fourth.

kind: specialist round — quarter obverse, the wig grooves
verdict_on_the_round: ACCEPTED, with a tone cost that came with its own diagnosis

the_measurement_that_decided_it: Pitch is not a free parameter and width is. D6 is a fraction of drawn LENGTH and stroke-width appears nowhere in it, so reaching the coin's 1.25-unit pitch needs 3.2x our cut length and takes D6 from 20.50% to 31.71% at 84px — forbidden. With pitch pinned, matching the coin's cut WIDTH and its DUTY CYCLE are different targets and only one is reachable. Duty wins, because at 84px a 0.35-unit cut is 0.29 device px and resolves nowhere: all that reaches a child is the mean, and the mean of a cut train is its duty. After: cut duty 0.322 against the coin's 0.258-0.429; ridge duty 0.348 against 0.350-0.443.
what_our_wig_was: Not a wide cut — a STRIPE PATTERN. At 2.5 wide on a 4.05 pitch there is no lit mass left between the marks to be cut, and the half-prominence finder scored 0 or 1 cuts on 7 of 7 lines: our own render could not be measured by the instrument that measures the coin. The overlay reads as a radiator.
THE_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MOST: D6 IS BLIND TO STROKE WIDTH. This round narrowed the exact defect D6 exists to catch by 2.6x and D6 moved by 0.0000 — judge-verified, 20.50% / 25.94% bit-identical before and after, drawn length and uniform length identical to the decimal. Meanwhile the only fix for the COUNT half of the same defect would raise D6 by 11 points. So D6 as implemented cannot route a width repair and actively forbids a count repair. That is a rubric fault of the same class as D7's, on the dimension section 14 exists to serve.

THE_INSTRUMENT_FAULT_THAT_INVALIDATES_A_.finding: _jw14cross.mjs's RIDGE duty is not a measurement of our lit rolls at all.
THE_INSTRUMENT_FAULT_THAT_INVALIDATES_A_.mechanism: A lit roll is a FLAT-TOPPED PLATEAU. A top wider than the 0.9u prominence window yields co-equal maxima, the "minimum" between them has the same grey, prominence is exactly 0.0, and the whole roll is discarded. Not the bracket-bound rule — the extrema finder meeting the prominence floor.
THE_INSTRUMENT_FAULT_THAT_INVALIDATES_A_.JUDGE_VERIFIED: Ran the round's own selection test. Of the six kept ridge candidates, ZERO sit on any of the five `base` rolls — the subject of this round. Three of the nine candidates are bare wig between cuts.
THE_INSTRUMENT_FAULT_THAT_INVALIDATES_A_.the_section_4_tell: Set every roll to 1.9, then to 1.1 — a 1.7x change on marks the transects demonstrably cross — and per-line ridge duty is BIT-IDENTICAL at 0.369/0.348/0.312, while CUT duty on the same two renders moves 0.316 -> 0.322. Two bit-identical answers from two different inputs.
THE_INSTRUMENT_FAULT_THAT_INVALIDATES_A_.WHAT_IS_RETRACTED: The published "ridge duty 0.348 against the coin's 0.350-0.443" (quarter round 9, and repeated by the JUDGE in two briefs and in BACKLOG/CHANGELOG) is computed over the two `fine` rolls and BARE WIG. It is not a statement about the lit rolls. The judge propagated it; the judge retracts it.
THE_INSTRUMENT_FAULT_THAT_INVALIDATES_A_.a_bridge_it_measured_rather_than_assumed: Comparing an authored width against a half-prominence duty needs a bridge, and it is NOT 1.0: measured 0.90x-1.53x, median 1.43x, because half prominence is taken against whatever shoulder the band has and a roll beside a cut has a much lower one. LEVELS carry that slack; the SIGN cannot — a positive multiplier cannot flip it, and the photometric sweep falls monotonically (0.322/0.277/0.233 at w 0.80/0.60/0.40) wherever the detector can see the rolls.
